Key Research Thinking Patterns: Large-Scale Empirical Stress-Testing: Systematically generating massive datasets of model outputs or network traffic to quantify failure rates and security vulnerabilities (e.g., Generating 576,000 code samples across 16 LLMs to quantify package hallucination rates and deploying global honeypots to measure reconnaissance attack volumes on Ethereum nodes).

Cross-Modal Metric Validation: Rigorously benchmarking automated computational metrics against human perceptual judgments to ensure alignment in AI-generated content and data analysis (e.g., Validating LPIPS and CLIP scores against subjective human rankings in image regeneration tasks and using ICC to assess inter-rater reliability in dataset value scoring).

Longitudinal Network Measurement and Taxonomy Development: Constructing comprehensive, time-series datasets and structured taxonomies to uncover hidden dynamics in complex, decentralized systems (e.g., Building MagnetDB from 28.6 million BitTorrent DHT entries to analyze piracy gift economies and developing the Dataset Value Taxonomy to operationalize epistemic value through Temporal Investment, Scale, and Accessibility).

Adversarial Simulation and Mitigation Strategy Evaluation: Simulating specific attack vectors to test system robustness and evaluating the efficacy of defensive mechanisms in real-world contexts (e.g., Simulating package confusion attacks to exploit LLM hallucinations and testing RAG and fine-tuning strategies to reduce hallucination rates while maintaining code quality).
Summary Description: Anindya Maiti is a principal investigator specializing in the intersection of AI security, decentralized network resilience, and data governance. His research focuses on securing the software supply chain against LLM-induced vulnerabilities, such as package hallucinations, and hardening P2P networks like Ethereum against targeted reconnaissance. Maiti employs large-scale empirical stress-testing, generating hundreds of thousands of code samples and deploying global honeypots to quantify threats. He also pioneers methodological frameworks for data stewardship, including the Dataset Value Taxonomy, and validates AI-generated content metrics against human perception. His work bridges technical cybersecurity with cultural analytics, utilizing longitudinal datasets like MagnetDB to understand digital piracy ecosystems. By integrating adversarial simulation, cross-modal metric validation, and rigorous network measurement, Maiti provides critical insights into securing AI-native environments and decentralized infrastructures, impacting fields from software engineering to digital humanities.
